name: PATH and the Java Classpath
overview: When Java says it can't find something, first ask what's missing. Learn to tell a lost command from a lost class and fix each one.

sections.title: Find the command
sections.content: Your shell uses PATH to locate java and javac. If the shell cannot find javac, check which JDK is installed and whether its bin directory is on PATH.

images.alt: Find the command or find the class?
images.caption: Check PATH for missing executables and the classpath for application classes and JARs.

sections.title: Find the class
sections.content: Java tools use the classpath to locate classes and libraries. Prefer an explicit -cp for manual runs, or let the build tool manage it. Add the current directory only if you need it.

sections.title: Read the failure
sections.content: ClassNotFoundException often follows an explicit class lookup. NoClassDefFoundError can indicate a missing runtime definition or an earlier initialization failure. Check the cause before changing settings.

keyPoints: Diagnose two failures. Check PATH when javac won't start, and check the runtime classpath or the original initialization error when a class won't load.

interviewQA.question: What separates classpath entries?
interviewQA.answer: Use a semicolon on Windows and a colon on Linux or macOS.

interviewQA.question: What should you check when javac is not recognized?
interviewQA.answer: Check the JDK installation and the shell’s PATH before looking at any Java classpath settings.
